title: Intermittent Network Microresponses: SDK Ergonomics PRD
content:
Goal: define an SDK surface and runtime behavior that makes Hosted API streaming useful on flaky / mobile / edge networks where disconnections, packet loss, and transient stalls are common. Deliver a low-friction developer experience for partial/microresponses, resumable sessions, and deterministic reconciliations so apps can remain interactive while preserving safety and observability.

Why this matters: many early customers embed streaming calls in mobile apps, browser clients with intermittent connectivity, and IoT devices. Today the UX degrades sharply on flaky networks: streams time out, clients must restart prompts losing context and tool outputs, and developers implement brittle retries. We need an SDK-first approach that handles:
- short partial outputs (microresponses) that can be committed locally
- deterministic resume so server and client converge after reconnect
- pragmatic backpressure and bandwidth adaptation for mobile
- simple tool-call semantics that avoid duplicate side effects on retries

Non-goals:
- full protocol redesign for server-to-server durable sessions (we assume hosted API server implements lightweight checkpoints).
- adding heavyweight cryptographic checkpoint proofs (out of scope for v1).

Success metrics (initial):
- 30% reduction in perceived session aborts for mobile beta customers (measured via client telemetry).
- <5% incidence of duplicate tool side-effects for resumed sessions during canary.
- Developer time-to-prototype for resume-enabled SDK flows < 2 hours (survey).

Principles:
1) Make partial outputs first-class: SDK exposes microresponse frames as a stream of stable, append-only segments that can be checkpointed.
2) Deterministic, idempotent resume: resume protocol must enable server to advance from a client checkpoint without re-running tool side-effects.
3) Minimal surface area for app authors: default heuristics should handle most cases; opt-in knobs for advanced apps.
4) Observable and debuggable: every resume, patch, and fallback should be telemetry-labeled and surfaced in Console.

User stories (examples):
- Mobile chat app: client receives partial reply segments while user reads; network drops; client reconnects and resumes; chat shows stable consolidated reply without duplicates.
- E-commerce agent: client invoked store-inventory tool; network blips during tool call; tool is executed exactly once even with resume.
- Offline note-taker: client collects microresponses while offline and uploads checkpoints when network returns; server merges deterministically.

High-level design:
A) Microresponse frames: small, typed frames emitted by the model runtime. Each frame includes: sequence_id, frame_type (text/markup/tool-call/commit), content_snippet (base64 safe for binary attachments), and cumulative_hash.
B) Checkpoints: clients can request an explicit checkpoint token from the server (checkpoint_id). The checkpoint represents an append-only offset plus a stable signature-like cumulative_hash used only for fast equality checks (not a cryptographic proof).
C) Resume semantics: on reconnect client sends last_checkpoint_id + list of unapplied local frames (if offline queuing). Server compares cumulative_hash and either: (1) fast-accept if hash matches, or (2) reconcile by returning delta frames and a new checkpoint. Tool executors on the server side switch to at-least-once guarded mode for ambiguous intervals: they accept resume tokens and use idempotency keys for side-effect deduplication.
D) Local commit model: SDK exposes commitCheckpoint() that upgrades local microresponses into a committed partial result visible to UI and retained for resuming.

SDK surface (sketch):
- startStream({prompt, sessionKey?, resumeToken?}) => StreamHandle
- StreamHandle.on('microresponse', (frame) => ... )
- StreamHandle.commitCheckpoint(label?) => Promise<checkpointId>
- StreamHandle.pause() / resume() => client-side backpressure controls
- StreamHandle.on('toolcall', async (toolSpec, context) => { return await runLocalAdapter(toolSpec) }) // hook for client proxies
- StreamHandle.resumeFrom(checkpointId, localFrames) => Promise<reconcileResult>

Default heuristics (out-of-the-box):
- Network drop detection: exponential backoff + fast reconnect attempts; immediate local checkpoint if reconnect latency > 2s
- Bandwidth-aware microresponses: compress text diffs; prefer short frames when measured RTT > 200ms
- Idle session GC: SDK holds soft state for 5 minutes by default; server session TTL configurable per-tier

Tool call safety model:
- Every tool invocation must be annotated with a developer-provided idempotency_key or SDK will synthesize one using sessionKey + sequence_id.
- Server must persist a short-lived idempotency entry until checkpoint is advanced beyond the tool call offset.
- On resume if server cannot prove tool execution status, it replies with tool_status: ambiguous and SDK presents a safe developer callback pattern to surface resolution (e.g., query tool state, show pending indicator).

Compact checkpoint format (example string payload):
- checkpoint_v1|session=abcd123|offset=17|hash=ef45c2b|meta=mobile-fast
- All checkpoints treated as opaque strings by SDK; server returns human-readable reasons in verbose mode.

Observability and Console integration: 
- Telemetry events: stream_start, microresponse_received, checkpoint_committed, resume_attempt, resume_reconcile, toolcall_status (ok/ambiguous/duplicate), gc_expiry
- Each event includes sessionKey, networkTag (wifi/cellular/unknown), clientLatencyMs, sampleFramesCount
- Console: new Session Playground that can replay microresponse frames, show checkpoint graph, and highlight ambiguous tool calls for support triage.

Developer ergonomics:
- Quickstart: 12-line mobile snippet demonstrating startStream + commitCheckpoint + automatic resume.
- Fallbacks: SDK exposes an easy hook to switch to synchronous non-streaming fallback for critical flows (e.g., payment confirmation) with minimal code changes.
- Testing harness: provide local simulator that injects disconnections and reorder frames so devs can iterate locally.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Alpha (internal, eng + 2 mobile partners): implement microresponses and checkpoint glue, coarse-grained idempotency, Console telemetry. Run chaos tests (disconnect-reconnect cycles).
- Beta (selected customers): expose SDK packages (iOS/Android/JS), capture metrics for duplicate tool effects and session abort rates, iterate heuristics.
- GA: refine TTL/backpressure defaults, provide migration guide, enable for all Hosted API customers behind feature flag.

Open questions / risks: 
- Storage window for idempotency metadata impacts cost — need SRE estimate for default TTLs.
- Edge-case: long-running tool calls that outlive checkpoints — define recommended patterns for long-running side effects.
- Security: checkpoints are opaque but leak minimal session metadata; confirm privacy review for telemetry fields.

Next steps / immediate action items: 
- Engineering: spike on lightweight checkpoint token (server) + SDK client proto by end of sprint (owner: Miguel).
- Product: recruit 2 mobile beta partners and craft test prompts (owner: Aisha).
- SRE / Infra: cost estimate for idempotency store (owner: Devon).
- Design / Docs: create quickstart and troubleshooting cheat sheet for SDK resume flows (owner: Samira).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic — aims to unblock mobile use cases quickly while keeping heavy durability for later phases. Looking for feedback on: default TTLs, syntactic shape of checkpoint token, and the UX around ambiguous tool statuses.
